limitations: Static review of the supplied text only. Tools were disabled and nothing was executed.

Only partition A was supplied as primary source. That is factory-receipt-archive.py lines 1-792, factory-reporting-policy.py lines 1-179 and factory-state-paths.py lines 1-165. I did not see factory-receipt-archive.py lines 793-1584 (B), factory-receipt-discovery.py or factory-receipts.py in full (C), or maintenance, reporting-receipts, digest and pr-discovery in full (D). This verdict says nothing about advance_origin, stage_projection, reconstruct_interval, coverage, PR discovery or the stage acknowledgement path.

The boundary excerpts of factory-receipts.py (36-75, 101-133) and factory-reporting-receipts.py (60-134) were read for context only. I found nothing concrete in them, but they get no full-file credit.

Not reviewed: factory-policy-observation.py (metadata.identity, timestamp, clock, decode, FIELDS), receipts.authenticate, receipts.receipt_artifact, receipts.annotate_reported_trust, coordinator.policy_hash and the contract helpers. Several checks here (observation field set, metadata digest coverage, historical authentication) depend on them.

The 2048-call and 32MiB bounds in _bootstrap_context, verify_bootstrap, projection_window and append_delivery are enforced as fail-closed errors. A long unchecked history or a large window can hit the bound and raise. I treated that as an explicit coverage gap, not a defect. I did not measure how often it triggers.

Origin authority rests on the reviewed approval file, the exclusive update-only App ruleset, and the writer's own checkpoint for the completed prefix. This review does not independently confirm those external GitHub settings or the operator observation sidecar.
The synthetic delivery adapter, the unfinished 1001 cadence acceptance, driver and workflow behavior, and activation are outside this packet, as stated.

What I checked, with the main line references:
- **Bootstrap and policy binding** (factory-receipt-archive.py:153-236). Schema v1 uses the raw ruleset digest. Schema v2 requires a sidecar whose identities match the approval exactly. - **Completed origin** (239-290, 752-790). The checkpoint binding and schema are validated. Ancestry is checked from bootstrap to frozen head to publication parent, and from publication to head. The walk only stops early at that certified frozen head.
- **History walk** (293-345, state-paths 66-165). Every non-bootstrap commit must have a single parent. Each edge is scanned with `scan_delta`, and the bootstrap tree gets a full `scan_tree`. `validate_entry` rejects submodules, bad modes, oversize blobs and paths outside the exact inert namespaces. The 256-commit and tree-page bounds fail closed. The ref and rulesets are re-read at the end.
- **Append CAS and lost acknowledgement** (428-560). The commit parent is the observed head and the PATCH uses `force: false`, so a competing advance is rejected as non-fast-forward. Any PATCH or acknowledgement failure sets `uncertain` and goes back through a fresh `verify_bootstrap`. An existing identity index is then validated against exact record, material and segment bytes and returned as already-appended. A competing different record at the same identity raises. A single shared byte budget covers source and state calls, and the write endpoints are an allow-list.
- **Projection window and retained lookup** (563-749). The frozen head must be an ancestor of the live head and descendant of bootstrap. Objects, materials, index and journal entries must be absent from the bootstrap tree, and index and segment cross-checks are enforced. Records are revalidated with `validate_record`, trust is annotated from the current trust file, and origin, approval and trust are re-verified before the result is returned. `coverage_complete` stays False, so no ready value grants authority.
- **Reporting policy** (factory-reporting-policy.py). Observations are bounded and canonicalized, and the binding, actor set, settle time and future-timestamp checks are consistent with `_bootstrap_context`.

Residual notes, none strong enough to report as defects:
- Some missing-object paths, such as a missing segment at line 516, would raise `TypeError` from `document(None)` instead of `ValueError`. They still fail closed.
